title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
summary: For an integer array nums, find the highest value of the bitwise XOR operation between any two elements nums[i] and nums[j] where i and j range from 0 to n-1.
statement: For an integer array nums, find the highest value of the bitwise XOR operation between any two elements nums[i] and nums[j] where i and j range from 0 to n-1.
constraints: Choose indices i <= j, so a single item may pair with itself. Return the maximum XOR value, not indices.
Repeated values are allowed. XOR is bitwise exclusive-or, not addition or exponentiation.
hints: A higher XOR bit outweighs every lower bit together.
Build the answer from high bits down, asking whether a candidate prefix can be formed by two input prefixes.
For each bit collect shifted prefixes; try (answer<<1)|1 and check whether prefix XOR candidate is also present.
The prefix-set identity a XOR b = candidate lets each feasibility test run in O(n); 31 bit positions give O(31n).
editorial: Suppose the optimal higher bits are fixed. Prefer setting the next bit if some pair of input prefixes achieves that extended candidate. A hash set checks the complementary prefix in constant expected time. Otherwise leave that bit zero. Lower bits cannot compensate for losing a feasible high bit. Use all 31 nonnegative signed-integer bits; a singleton correctly yields zero.

tests.explanation: 5 XOR 25 = 28 is largest; pairing the largest numbers by numeric size need not maximize XOR.
The only allowed pair uses the same index twice, and 7 XOR 7 is 0.
